ordered_diagnoses: Multisystem Langerhans cell histiocytosis with Erdheim-Chester-like features

s1.syndrome_frame: Multisystem disorder with chronic skin lesions and endocrine abnormalities
salient_findings: Numerous asymptomatic reddish-brownish papules, nodules, and plaques over the whole body
Central diabetes insipidus, growth retardation, and hypothyroidism
key_facts: 7-year medical history of skin lesions
Skin lesions began on bilateral eyelid margins and extended to trunk and extremities
Patient has central diabetes insipidus
Patient has growth retardation
Patient has hypothyroidism
Skin biopsy showed dense granulomatous infiltrate in the upper dermis
Immunohistochemical results were negative for CD1a and S-100, positive for CD68

Skin lesions are present on periocular areas, perioral areas, neck, shoulder, axillary folds, cubital fossa, wrists, palms, umbilical region, lateral abdomen, inguinal area, anogenital area, popliteal fossa, and ankles

shortlist: Multisystem Langerhans cell histiocytosis with Erdheim-Chester-like features

shortlist.label: Erdheim-Chester disease
shortlist.why_kept: Matches case facts of chronic skin lesions, central diabetes insipidus, and granulomatous infiltrate on skin biopsy

shortlist.label: Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with skin lesions, diabetes insipidus, and growth retardation, although immunohistochemical results were negative for CD1a and S-100

shortlist.label: Xanthoma disseminatum
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by widespread skin lesions and can involve the central nervous system, but less likely given the granulomatous infiltrate and negative CD1a and S-100 results

shortlist.label: Necrobiotic xanthogranuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Presents with skin lesions and can have systemic involvement, including paraproteinemia, but less likely given the clinical presentation and biopsy findings

shortlist.label: Multisystem Langerhans cell histiocytosis with Erdheim-Chester-like features
shortlist.why_kept: Combines features of Langerhans cell histiocytosis and Erdheim-Chester disease, making it a plausible diagnosis given the case facts

raw.rationale: The patient's 7-year medical history of skin lesions, central diabetes insipidus, growth retardation, and hypothyroidism, along with the skin biopsy showing a dense granulomatous infiltrate and immunohistochemical results positive for CD68, are consistent with Erdheim-Chester disease, a rare form of non-Langerhans cell histiocytosis.

rejected.label: Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis
rejected.why: Immunohistochemical results were negative for CD1a and S-100, which are typically positive in Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis

rejected.label: Xanthoma disseminatum
rejected.why: Skin lesions in Xanthoma disseminatum are typically more yellowish and less granulomatous than those described in the patient

rejected.label: Necrobiotic xanthogranuloma
rejected.why: This condition is more commonly associated with paraproteinemia and does not typically present with the systemic symptoms described in the patient

rejected.label: Multisystem Langerhans cell histiocytosis with Erdheim-Chester-like features
rejected.why: The immunohistochemical results and clinical presentation are more consistent with Erdheim-Chester disease than a multisystem Langerhans cell histiocytosis with Erdheim-Chester-like features
